Subject: GPU guidance request — latency targets + long-context RAG

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving into sizing for a Dedicated engagement and need a concrete recommendation on GPU SKUs. High level constraints:
- Use cases: conversational clinical assistant (chat) with RAG back-end, and high-volume embedding requests for search indexing.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency target ~50–80ms (for short chats ~512 tokens).
- Throughput: steady-state ~1,200 chat requests/minute (peak burst ~3k/min), embeddings ~600/min.
- Average expected turn length: 150 tokens (chat), but some sessions use long context up to 32k tokens for full patient history retrieval.
- Model goals: prefer a 70B-parameter LLM family (FP16/quantized variants) for chat; embeddings on smaller distilled models.
- Security/compliance: procurement will require SOC2 evidence and a security questionnaire (attached).

Question: for Dedicated, should we size primarily with H100s, A100s, or L4s (or a hybrid)? We're trying to balance unit cost vs meeting latency for long-context sessions and the cost of reserved capacity.

I've attached our SLO/requirements doc (flux_slo_requirements.pdf). Can you send an opinionated starting footprint and a short rationale we can take to procurement?

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Head of AI Platform

Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and the SLO doc. Below is a concise, pragmatic set of heuristics and a recommended starter footprint for Dedicated. I'll follow up with an ops note and a small cost workbook.

Quick TL;DR recommendation: start with a hybrid pool — reserved H100 capacity to cover long-context and high-concurrency chat paths, backed by a larger L4 burst pool for embeddings and cheaper short-chat inference. Use A100s only if you have legacy model artifacts tied to that stack or need an intermediate price-performance tradeoff for specific quantized variants.

Why (heuristics):
- H100 (80GB / NVLink): best for memory-hungry models and 32k-context workloads. If you need to run a sharded 70B with 32k context without heavy offloading, H100 is the most predictable option for p95 latency at low batch sizes. Cost is highest per GPU but you avoid excessive model parallel overhead and CPU/GPU cross-traffic.
- A100 (80GB / 40GB variants): solid middle ground. Good for many 70B deployments if you can accept model partitioning overhead and slightly higher tail latency at low batch sizes. If you already have optimized kernels targeting A100, it can reduce engineering uplift.
- L4 (16GB / 32GB-ish inference accelerators): lowest unit cost, optimized for quantized INT8/FP8 workloads. Excellent for dense embeddings and low-latency short-chat at scale. Not a fit for 32k-context 70B without aggressive model truncation/LLM distillation; expect either higher latency or reduced context capacity.

Sizing heuristics and numbers (starter footprint):
- Baseline assumptions: average chat request uses 150 tokens output, 150 tokens input; embedding request cost is ~0.2 of a chat request in compute. KV/prefix cache expected to reduce repeated-work by ~30% for multi-turn flows.
- Conservative reserved pool (initial):
  * H100s: 4 x H100-80GB reserved (handles long-context 70B sharded runs, supports steady-state chat p95 and provides headroom for peaks assuming prefix caching and smallish batch sizes).
  * L4s: 40 x L4 instances reserved for embeddings and short-chat; useful to offload ~70% of inference volume and keep unit cost down.
  * Autoscaling burst: allow additional L4 burst capacity up to 120 nodes and conversion of some A100 or H100 capacity as fallback in emergencies.
- Expected operational outcome: with this mix, ~70–80% of traffic (by request count) can be served on L4 at favorable cost; H100 handles the 32k-context sessions and the heavier chat tails.

Performance/cost tradeoffs:
- If you target 50ms p95 for short chats, prewarmed L4 nodes with small batch sizes and low cold starts are efficient; for long-context p95 you will need the H100 pool and controlled concurrency to avoid queuing.
- Quantization (INT8 / NF4) drives L4 viability; if your chat model tolerates aggressive quant, L4 becomes attractive for more of the traffic.

Operational notes (quick wins):
- Enable prefix/KV caching for patient histories to cut token computation and reduce H100 use by ~25–40% on multi-turn sessions.
- Reserve a small number of prewarmed H100s (the 4 above) pinned to the model version to avoid cold-start variance on tail latency.
- Configure autoscaler with a small buffer for p95 headroom (e.g., 10–15% capacity headroom) rather than reactive-only scale-ups.

Next steps:
1) We will send a short cost workbook showing expected monthly cost for the 4H100 + 40L4 reserved footprint (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop to align on concurrency profiles and model quantization tolerance.
3) We'll provide SOC2 evidence and a security contact for procurement (Aditya will follow up).

If you want a single-line action to send to procurement: “Recommend reserved: 4x H100-80GB, 40x L4 (reserve), autoscaler with 120-node L4 burst, SOC2 evidence attached. See Redwood cost workbook.”

—Dylan

Quick ops notes to add to Dylan's recommendation:

- Autoscaling policies: use a two-tier autoscaler — fast L4 horizontal scaling (seconds) for embeddings and short-chat, slower H100 scale events with predictive windowing (minutes) for long-context sessions. Tie scale decisions to queue length + token-rate metrics rather than CPU alone.
- Warmed model slots: pin the most used model variants to a small subset of H100 nodes to avoid token-generation warmup variance.
- Quantization/FFI: for RAG-heavy flows, use mixed strategy: run the retriever + dense embed on L4, run the generator on H100; where possible use 4-bit for generator to reduce memory.
- Fallthroughs: plan for automatic model fallback to a smaller quantized variant on L4 when H100 capacity is constrained.

I'll own the SOC2 contact and will get the security pack to procurement.

Cheers,
